name: anti-rea
description: AI Agent-callable code-protection toolchain that raises the cost of automated reverse engineering (REA) for code you own. LLVM-based obfuscation transforms + CLI + MCP server. Phased workflow: read-only survey -> transformation proposal for user review -> user picks a mode (one-shot build / build-architecture transformation with an anti-REA build environment) -> flexible execution. Provides information and methodology; does not auto-modify the target project's build system.

doctor.description: Environment self-check; fast-fails with guidance when a required component is missing.

mcp.description: MCP server exposing the tools below over stdio JSON-RPC.

workflow.principle: Do not auto-modify the target project's build system. Provide information + methodology + commands; the agent works in phases with the user, and each phase ends with something reviewable before proceeding.

phases.name: survey
outputs: build profile (entry point, compiler selection, artifact form, deps, CI, self-tests)

phases.name: proposal
outputs: proposal: scope, build profile, dependency/environment install list, recommended mode + rationale, step-by-step plan, verification & rollback
phases.gate: user approval required before any change

phases.name: decide
actions: user picks mode A (one-shot build) / B (transform build architecture + anti-REA build environment) / C (A then B)

phases.name: execute
actions: mode B: buildenv + inject clang+plugin into the project's own build (CC wrapper / toolchain file / build script edits)
rules: show diffs of any build-file change to the user before applying
adapt injection to the project's build system (autoconf/Make/CMake/Meson/Cargo/node-gyp/Bazel/scripted)
report honestly if a dependency cannot be installed

phases.name: verify
actions: anti-rea attack_sim (--allow-llm for real LLM red-team sessions)
outputs: verification report, eval report, human-readable report, rollback/rebuild instructions

modes.A: one-shot build: no changes to the target project; protect produces standalone baseline/protected artifacts under out/
modes.B: build-architecture transformation: inject the compiler wrapper into the project's own build (e.g. CC=anti-rea-cc after sourcing buildenv scope.env), producing native artifacts (.so etc.) and a reusable anti-REA build environment (script/make target/CI job)
modes.C: A then B: first validate policy/cost with a one-shot build, then transform the build architecture

java_anti_rea.note: Java/Android has no LLVM IR transforms; the skill provides a selectable option menu (principles, pros/cons/impacts, sources and usage) and lets the user choose. Third-party tools and commercial hardening products are NOT bundled or downloaded by this skill -- only their sources and usage are recorded.

options.name: server-side logic (core algorithms/keys stay off the client)
shrink + name obfuscation (ProGuard / R8 / yGuard; baseline)
string/constant encryption + control-flow obfuscation (commercial or in-house)
bytecode virtualization (VMP-style; highest single-point cost on the Java layer)
offload sensitive core to native (JNI / JNA / Panama FFM) then harden with this skill

verification.note: verify/attack_sim target LLVM native artifacts and do NOT apply to Java bytecode; use decompilers (jadx/CFR/Vineflower) per the guide's methodology.

dotnet_anti_rea.note: .NET (C#/F#/VB; including Unity, MAUI, Blazor, desktop/CLI/services) has no IL-level transforms; the skill provides a selectable option menu (D0-D8) with principles, pros/cons/impacts, sources and usage. Third-party tools and commercial hardening products are NOT bundled or downloaded by this skill -- only their sources and usage are recorded. NativeAOT / IL2CPP / native-offload outputs can be hardened with this skill's regular native pipeline.

options.name: server-side logic (core algorithms/keys stay off the client)
trim + name obfuscation (Obfuscar / ConfuserEx / Dotfuscator; baseline)
IL virtualization (VMP-style; highest single-point cost on the IL layer)
offload sensitive core to native (P/Invoke / C++-CLI / function pointers) then harden with this skill
NativeAOT / Mono AOT (whole-app AOT; closed-world + per-RID)

unity.note: Mono builds are decompiled directly; IL2CPP removes IL but global-metadata.dat can be recovered (Il2CppDumper). IL2CPP generates readable C++ -- this skill's build injection (clang + plugin) can harden it selectively; validate on your Unity version first.

verification.note: verify/attack_sim target LLVM native artifacts and do NOT apply to CIL managed assemblies; decompile/cross-check with ILSpy/ilspycmd + dnSpyEx + dotPeek and run de4dot to test real strength. Native parts (D5/D6/IL2CPP) use the regular native pipeline.

tools.name: anti_rea.scan
tools.description: Scan a project and produce an asset manifest (asset_manifest schema). Read-only, idempotent.

tools.name: anti_rea.plan
tools.description: Generate a protection policy from a manifest, under a performance budget.

tools.name: anti_rea.protect
tools.description: Apply transforms per policy; produces protected artifacts + transform log (deterministic per seed).

tools.name: anti_rea.attack_sim
tools.description: Attack simulation (static/dynamic/cross-version). Read-only, idempotent; LLM egress requires allow_llm.

tools.name: anti_rea.evolve
tools.description: Genetic strategy evolution (DEAP); returns the best policy and fitness.

provisioning.principle: Ship only the skill's own source. Never bundle, pre-install or auto-download third-party tools; record their sources and usage instead, and let the user install them when the chosen language / mode / feature requires it. Minimal install by default; fetch everything else on demand.

T1.name: native transforms (on demand)
T1.when: mode A/B selected AND own native code (C/C++, Rust C/FFI sources, Python C extensions) is to be transformed: protect / verify / attack_sim
components: `make build` compiles this skill's pass from source
T1.install: user-provided system packages; then run `make build`

T2.name: language & platform extensions (on demand)
T2.when: depends on the target language / build system / host platform
components: JDK + build tools (Java/Android survey - use the target project's own toolchain)
container runtime (host platform mismatch, or no LLVM on the host)

T3.name: optional enhancements (on demand, at the latest)
T3.when: only when the corresponding feature is used
T3.install: pip install -r requirements-optional.txt  # evolve only; the rest are user-provided

T4.name: never shipped
components: Java/Android third-party hardening tools/products: ProGuard, R8, yGuard, Zelix KlassMaster, Allatori, DashO, DexGuard, GraalVM, jadx, CFR, Vineflower
T4.install: user-provided; sources and usage only (see docs/java-anti-rea.md)

deferral_rules: Install T0 only during P0 survey; do not install LLVM, pull images or download Ghidra before the user has chosen a mode.
In the P1 proposal, list components in three buckets: install now (T0) / install after the mode is chosen (T1) / install only if the feature is used (T2/T3).
Read only SKILL.md plus the one guide relevant to the chosen language/mode; do not ingest docs/ wholesale (token cost).
Ask for user confirmation before installing system packages, pulling images or downloading third-party tools; the user owns tool licenses and credentials.
If a component cannot be installed, report it honestly instead of silently substituting or pretending success.

requirements.policy: Minimal by default (T0). Optional components are installed only when the chosen language/mode/feature needs them; third-party tools are never bundled or downloaded by this skill. See `provisioning` and docs/PROVISIONING.md.

optional.deap: >=1.4 - T3, only for `anti-rea evolve` (pip install -r requirements-optional.txt)
optional.ghidra: >=12 with PyGhidra (set ANTI_REA_GHIDRA=1 for independent verification) - T3, user-provided
optional.rustc_cargo: for Rust C/FFI-source pilot - T2, user-provided
optional.node_npm: for JS/TS scanning only - T2, user-provided

environment_variables.ANTI_REA_GHIDRA: set to 1 to enable Ghidra independent verification

platforms.note: scan/plan run anywhere Python does; protect requires a built LLVM pass plugin and is validated on linux-x86_64 only.

languages.java_note: No IR transforms for Java bytecode; see the top-level `java_anti_rea` option menu (docs/java-anti-rea.md), and let the user choose the combination. Kotlin/Scala compile to JVM bytecode and follow the same menu.
languages.dotnet_note: No IL transforms for .NET (C#/F#/VB) or Unity; see the top-level `dotnet_anti_rea` option menu (docs/dotnet-anti-rea.md). NativeAOT/IL2CPP/native-offload outputs go through the regular native pipeline.

quickstart: pip install -r requirements.txt   # minimal (T0): scan/plan/doctor/report work with no compiler
anti-rea doctor                  # grouped by provisioning tier; shows what to install for which feature
# install the rest on demand only: LLVM/clang 18 + cmake + binutils (T1, for protect/verify), see docs/PROVISIONING.md

# mode B (native artifacts like .so): anti-rea buildenv out/protection_policy.yaml --root <project> --protect-all -o out/scope.env; source out/scope.env; export CC=<repo>/integrations/cc-wrapper/anti-rea-cc; <build the project as usual>
# before changing anything in the target project, follow the phased workflow in SKILL.md: P0 survey -> P1 proposal (user review) -> P2 mode choice -> P3 execute -> P4 verify
